# lccc option inventory

Which options the compiler driver implements, tolerates or refuses, and the evidence for each.
Every row is re-measured against a built `lccc` by `python3 scripts/lccc_options_inventory.py --check`,
so this table cannot drift from the binary: a row whose measured behaviour differs from its class,
or a document that differs from the table, fails the check.  The driver's policy is described at the
top of `src/driver/cli.rs`; an option that is not listed here is governed by that policy's default
(an unknown `-f` or `-W` option is accepted with a warning, an unknown `-m` option is an error).

Regenerate with `python3 scripts/lccc_options_inventory.py --write` after changing the table.

## Implemented

Accepted **and** observed to do what it says.  The *Effect* column names the evidence.

| Option | Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `-O2 -fno-plt -fPIC` | calls through the GOT (`call *f@GOTPCREL`) instead of the PLT | reloc: `R_X86_64_GOTPCRELX\s+puts` |
| `-fvisibility=hidden` | defined symbols get `STV_HIDDEN` | syms: `GLOBAL\s+HIDDEN\s+\d+\s+f$` |
| `-O2 -ftrapv` | signed overflow checked; the failing path calls `abort` | asm: `call\s+abort@PLT` |
| `-O2 -fstack-clash-protection` | frames over a page are probed page by page (`orl $0, (%rsp)`) | asm: `orl\s+\$0,\s+\(%rsp\)` |
| `-m32 -O2 -fstack-clash-protection` | same probing on i686 (`orl $0, (%esp)`) | asm: `orl\s+\$0,\s+\(%esp\)` |
| `-O2 -fstack-protector-all` | canary load from `%fs:40` and a `__stack_chk_fail` call | asm: `%fs:40`; `__stack_chk_fail` |
| `-O2 -fstack-protector-all -mstack-protector-guard=tls -mstack-protector-guard-reg=gs -mstack-protector-guard-offset=64` | kernel-style guard location (`%gs:64`) | asm: `%gs:64`; absent `%fs:40` |
| `-O2 -fstack-protector-all -mstack-protector-guard=tls -mstack-protector-guard-symbol=__stack_chk_guard` | guard read from a named TLS symbol | asm: `%fs:__stack_chk_guard` |
| `-m32 -O2 -fstack-protector-all` | i686 canary from `%gs:20` | asm: `%gs:20` |
| `-O2 -fcf-protection=full` | every function starts with `endbr64` | asm: `endbr64` |
| `-O1 -fpack-struct` | struct members are packed (`sizeof` 5, not 8) | asm: `movl\s+\$5,\s+%eax` |
| `-O1 -funsigned-char` | plain `char` is unsigned (`c < 0` folds to 0) | asm: `xorl\s+%eax,\s+%eax` |
| `-fshort-wchar` | `wchar_t` is 2 bytes | macros: `__SIZEOF_WCHAR_T__ 2` |
| `-ffast-math` | defines `__FAST_MATH__` | macros: `__FAST_MATH__ 1` |
| `-madx -mrdseed -mclwb -mfsgsbase -mrdpid` | the scalar and system ISA options define GCC's macros (their intrinsics are in `x86gprintrin.h`; all 28 options are held to GCC by `check_x86_mflag_macros.py`) | macros: `__ADX__ 1`; `__RDSEED__ 1`; `__CLWB__ 1`; `__FSGSBASE__ 1`; `__RDPID__ 1` |
| `-march=skylake -mno-adx` | a CPU's extensions are announced and an explicit `-mno-` removes one | macros: `__RDSEED__ 1`; `__XSAVEC__ 1`; absent `__ADX__` |
| `-O2 -pg` | function entry calls `mcount` / `__fentry__` | asm: `mcount\|__fentry__` |
| `-O2 -fno-omit-frame-pointer` | keeps the frame pointer (`pushq %rbp`) | asm: `pushq\s+%rbp` |
| `-O2 -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables` | no `.cfi_*` unwind directives | asm: absent `\.cfi_startproc` |
| `-O2 -fpatchable-function-entry=2` | two `nop`s at entry and a `__patchable_function_entries` record | asm: `__patchable_function_entries`; `^\s*nop$` |
| `-g -O0` | emits DWARF sections (`.debug_line`, `.debug_info`) | sections: `\.debug_line`; `\.debug_info` |
| `-Wall -Wextra` | `-Wformat`, `-Wunused-variable` and `-Wsign-compare` report | diag: `\[-Wformat`; `-Wunused-variable`; `-Wsign-compare` |
| `-nostdlib -Wl,--build-id` | `.note.gnu.build-id` is emitted | notes: `Build ID` |
| `-nostdlib -Wl,--image-base=0x10000000` | entry point moves to the requested base | header: `Entry point address:\s+0x1000` |
| `-nostdlib -Wl,-z,max-page-size=65536` | `PT_LOAD` alignment becomes 0x10000 | segments: `LOAD.*\s0x10000\s*$` |
| `-nostdlib -fPIE -pie -Wl,-z,pack-relative-relocs` | relative relocations are packed (`DT_RELR`) | dynamic: `\(RELR\)` |
| `-nostdlib -O1 -ffunction-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -Wl,--icf=all` | identical functions share one address | symbols: `:\s+([0-9a-f]{16})\s+\d+ FUNC\s+GLOBAL\s+DEFAULT\s+\d+\s+fa\n.*:\s+\1\s+\d+ FUNC\s+GLOBAL\s+DEFAULT\s+\d+\s+fb` |

## Tolerated

Accepted with a warning; the compiler does nothing with it.  Builds that pass these options keep working, but get none of the behaviour.  `LCCC_STRICT_OPTIONS=1` turns them into errors.

| Option | Behaviour | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `-Wshadow` | no shadowing diagnostics are produced | `tolerated but not implemented` |
| `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` | no maybe-uninitialized diagnostics are produced | `tolerated but not implemented` |
| `-gz` | debug sections are not compressed | `not supported` |
| `-fxyzzy-lccc-control` | unknown `-f` options are accepted with a warning (negative control) | `tolerated but not implemented` |
| `-Wxyzzy-lccc-control` | unknown `-W` options are accepted with a warning (negative control) | `tolerated but not implemented` |

## Refused

A hard error, because accepting it silently would change what the artifact is (security hardening, output format, runtime) without telling the user.

| Option | Behaviour | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `-static-pie` | no static PIE output | `-static-pie is not supported` |
| `-flto` | no link-time optimization | `LTO IR production and link-time consumption are not implemented` |
| `-fsanitize=address` | no sanitizer runtime | `-fsanitize=address is not supported` |
| `-ftest-coverage` | no `.gcno`/`.gcda` output | `-ftest-coverage is not implemented` |
| `-mstackrealign` | no stack realignment | `unsupported machine option -mstackrealign` |
| `-m32 -nostdlib -Wl,--emit-relocs` | the i686 linker cannot retain relocations | `--emit-relocs is not supported by the elf_i386` |
| `-m32 -muintr` | user interrupts exist in 64-bit code only (GCC's words) | `'-muintr' not supported for 32-bit code` |
| `-mxop` | no XOP code generation and no XOP intrinsics, so no `__XOP__` | `unsupported machine option -mxop` |
| `-mxyzzy-lccc-control` | unknown `-m` options are errors (negative control) | `unsupported machine option` |
